about: Reasons for blocks that tools/s4/lift_extra.py registered before it required
one. Its --entry path took `args.why[k] if k < len(args.why) else ""`, so an
--entry without a matching --why was lifted silently with an empty reason.
Two of 958 rows were in that state; the tool now refuses.
Each reason below was RECOVERED from surviving run evidence, not written from
memory, and each says where it came from. That recovery was only possible
because those runs happened to still be on disk, which is the argument for
the record rather than a reassurance about it.
This file should never grow. A new row with no reason is now a hard failure

rows.why: a guest thread start routine: CreateThread targets it, so a created thread has nowhere to begin unless it is lifted as its own module
rows.recovered: Documentation/receipts/s4-suspension-and-fls-v1.json records it as `guest_start_routine` for a created thread, one of eight distinct start routines that receipt names. It is also the address the S4 slice-12 journal tabulates while diagnosing the process-wide FLS defect.
rows.owner: inside FUN_007c5820 (0x007c5820..0x007c5950), so it is a mid-function entry rather than a function the map missed

rows.why: a dispatch target the function table had no row for: a driven run ended on it, so it is lifted as its own module to give the table an entry
rows.recovered: private/generated/s4/run/sus6.matrix.json records the run `sus6.on` ending with `exit_pc: 0x007ebb90` and the note `function table miss at 0x007ebb90 (region .text, table 21953/65536 entries)`, during the suspension and FLS investigation.
rows.owner: inside FUN_007ebb40 (0x007ebb40..0x007ebc80), so it is a mid-function entry rather than a function the map missed
